ENVIRONMENT
- C++ reference binary (ground truth): /workspace/dataset/test11_executable
- Rust port under test:                /output/test11
- Rust source lives in /output (test11.rs, src/lib.rs, src/idna/*.rs). You may READ it.
- The C++ library source (idna.hpp / idna.cpp) does NOT exist on disk. Do not look for it.

HARD RULES
- You MUST NOT modify, create, or delete anything under /output. Read-only there.
- Do all scratch work under your own private scratch dir; create it with
  mkdir -p and use a path unique to you (given below). Never write to /tmp root directly.
- Both binaries take the SAME argv. Compare raw bytes of stdout AND the exit code.
- Compare with byte-exact tooling (cmp, or diff on files, or shell string equality on
  command substitution ONLY when you know there are no trailing-newline subtleties).
  Prefer writing stdout to files and using 'cmp -s'.
- Arguments may contain spaces, quotes, newlines, NUL-adjacent bytes, and invalid UTF-8.
  Quote your shell variables properly ("$x", not $x).
- Report ONLY real, reproduced divergences. If you cannot reproduce it twice, it is not
  a finding. Do not speculate about code you did not execute.

Your private scratch dir: /tmp/wf-fuzz-r1-6

TASK — differential fuzzing, round 1, strategy "case-folding".

Your assigned angle:
Case folding stress: all-upper, all-lower, alternating, non-ASCII uppercase whose lowercase differs in Unicode (Ä, Σ, İ, Ǆ), German ß, Turkish dotless i, full-width Latin letters, and ASCII letters adjacent to high bytes.

Write a shell (or python3) driver in your scratch dir that, for each generated input,
runs both binaries with that input as a single argv element, captures stdout to
separate files, and compares them with 'cmp -s'. Also compare exit codes. Print only
the mismatches, plus a final total of cases executed.

Generate inputs PROGRAMMATICALLY so you can cover hundreds to thousands of cases.
Use printf with escapes (e.g. printf '\xff') or python3 to build byte sequences, and
pass them via a shell array or python subprocess with a list argv — never by
re-splitting a string. python3 + subprocess.run([...], capture_output=True) with
bytes arguments (os.fsencode / bytes objects) is the most reliable route for
arbitrary bytes; prefer it.



Report every reproduced divergence with an exact repro command. If you find none,
say so honestly with divergenceCount 0 — a clean result is a useful result, and
inventing a finding is much worse than reporting none. In notes, state what you
deliberately did NOT cover so a later reviewer can pick it up.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Differential fuzzer, round 1, strategy: case-folding.

Runs /workspace/dataset/test11_executable (ground truth) and /output/test11
with identical argv (raw bytes), compares stdout byte-exactly and exit codes.
"""
import os
import subprocess
import sys

CPP = b"/workspace/dataset/test11_executable"
RUST = b"/output/test11"
SCRATCH = "/tmp/wf-fuzz-r1-6"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- generators

def u(cp):
    return chr(cp).encode("utf-8")


CASES = []          # list of (label, [argbytes, ...])
_seen = set()


def add(label, *args):
    key = tuple(args)
    if key in _seen:
        return
    _seen.add(key)
    CASES.append((label, list(args)))


# --- 1. every single byte alone, and in ASCII-letter contexts -------------
CONTEXTS = [
    b"%s",
    b"A%s",
    b"%sA",
    b"A%sB",
    b"a%sb",
    b"Z%sz",
    b"%s.COM",
    b"EXAM%sPLE.CoM",
    b"xn--%sA",
    b"XN--%sA",
    b"%s%s",
]
for b in range(1, 256):
    bb = bytes([b])
    for i, tpl in enumerate(CONTEXTS):
        arg = tpl.replace(b"%s", bb)
        add("byte-0x%02x-ctx%d" % (b, i), arg)

# --- 2. ASCII letters adjacent to high bytes (pairs) ---------------------
HIGH = [0x80, 0x9f, 0xa0, 0xbf, 0xc0, 0xc2, 0xc3, 0xc4, 0xcf, 0xdf,
        0xe0, 0xe1, 0xed, 0xef, 0xf0, 0xf4, 0xf5, 0xfe, 0xff]
LETTERS = [b"A", b"Z", b"a", b"z", b"I", b"i", b"S", b"s", b"K", b"k",
           b"@", b"[", b"`", b"{", b"0", b"9", b".", b"-"]
for h in HIGH:
    hb = bytes([h])
    for L in LETTERS:
        add("adj-%02x-%s" % (h, L.hex()), hb + L)
        add("adj-%s-%02x" % (L.hex(), h), L + hb)
        add("adj-%02x-%s-%02x" % (h, L.hex(), h), hb + L + hb)
        add("adj-%s-%02x-%s" % (L.hex(), h, L.hex()), L + hb + L)

# --- 3. all-upper / all-lower / alternating / inverted of base domains ---
BASES = [
    "example.com", "test.example.com", "localhost", "xn--example.com",
    "xn--fiq228c.com", "straße.de", "ÄÖÜ.de", "ΣΊΣΥΦΟΣ.gr", "İstanbul.tr",
    "ǄǅǆǇǈǉǊǋǌ.hr", "ＡＢＣ.ＣＯＭ", "ＦＵＬＬＷＩＤＴＨ.ｊｐ",
    "ΟΔΟΣ.gr", "ΑΣ.gr", "ıI.tr", "Iı.tr", "İi.tr", "ii̇.tr",
    "ＭｉＸｅＤ.Ｃｏｍ", "ÀÁÂÃÄÅÆÇÈÉ.fr", "ÊËÌÍÎÏÐÑÒÓ.fr",
    "ÔÕÖØÙÚÛÜÝÞ.fr", "ΆΈΉΊΌΎΏ.gr", "ЁЂЃЄЅІЇЈЉЊ.ru",
    "АБВГДЕЖЗИЙ.ru", "ΪΫάέήί.gr", "ǅǈǋ.hr", "ﬀﬁﬂﬃﬄﬅﬆ.lig",
    "ΩKÅ.unit", "ΩＫÅ.unit", "ẛ.long-s", "ẞ.de", "ß.de", "SS.de",
    "ⅠⅡⅢⅣⅤ.roman", "ⅰⅱⅲⅳⅴ.roman", "ᾼῌῼ.gr", "ᾈᾉᾊ.gr",
    "ⓐⒶ.circ", "ᏸᏹᏺ.chr", "ႠႡႢ.geo", "ⴀⴁⴂ.geo",
    "𐐀𐐁𐐂.des", "𐐨𐐩𐐪.des", "Ꞌꞌꟼ.misc", "ᵽᵾᵿ.misc",
]
for s in BASES:
    raw = s.encode("utf-8")
    add("base", raw)
    add("upper", s.upper().encode("utf-8"))
    add("lower", s.lower().encode("utf-8"))
    add("casefold", s.casefold().encode("utf-8"))
    add("swapcase", s.swapcase().encode("utf-8"))
    add("title", s.title().encode("utf-8"))
    # byte-wise alternating ASCII case
    alt = bytearray(raw)
    for i in range(len(alt)):
        if 0x41 <= alt[i] <= 0x5A and i % 2 == 0:
            alt[i] += 32
        elif 0x61 <= alt[i] <= 0x7A and i % 2 == 1:
            alt[i] -= 32
    add("bytealt", bytes(alt))
    # every byte of the UTF-8 form flipped through ASCII case fold manually
    add("prefixed", b"xn--" + raw)
    add("PREFIXED", b"XN--" + raw)
    add("Prefixed", b"Xn--" + raw)
    add("prEfixed", b"xN--" + raw)
    add("dbl-prefixed", b"xn--xn--" + raw)

# --- 4. specific code points whose case mapping is non-trivial ----------
TRICKY_CPS = [
    0x00C4, 0x00E4,          # A/a diaeresis
    0x00DF, 0x1E9E,          # sharp s, capital sharp s
    0x0130, 0x0131,          # I dot above, dotless i
    0x0049, 0x0069,          # I, i
    0x01C4, 0x01C5, 0x01C6,  # DZ caron trio
    0x01C7, 0x01C8, 0x01C9,
    0x01CA, 0x01CB, 0x01CC,
    0x03A3, 0x03C3, 0x03C2,  # Sigma, sigma, final sigma
    0x0345, 0x0399, 0x1FBE,  # ypogegrammeni / iota
    0x212A, 0x212B, 0x2126,  # Kelvin, Angstrom, Ohm
    0x0130, 0x0307,          # combining dot above
    0xFF21, 0xFF3A, 0xFF41, 0xFF5A,   # fullwidth A Z a z
    0xFF10, 0xFF0E, 0xFF0D,           # fullwidth 0 . -
    0x0132, 0x0133, 0x0149,
    0x017F,                  # long s
    0x1E96, 0x1E97, 0x1E98, 0x1E99, 0x1E9A,
    0x1F88, 0x1F80, 0x1FFC,
    0x0587, 0x0535, 0x0582,
    0x10400, 0x10428,        # Deseret
    0x104B0, 0x104D8,        # Osage
    0x1E900, 0x1E922,        # Adlam
    0x13A0, 0xAB70,          # Cherokee
    0x2170, 0x2160,
    0x1FD3, 0x1FE3,
    0x00B5, 0x03BC, 0x039C,  # micro / mu
    0x1E9B,
    0xA7C7, 0xA7C8,
    0x0250, 0x2C6F,
]
for cp in TRICKY_CPS:
    ch = u(cp)
    add("cp-%04X" % cp, ch)
    add("cp-%04X-dom" % cp, ch + b".com")
    add("cp-%04X-DOM" % cp, ch + b".COM")
    add("cp-%04X-mixA" % cp, b"A" + ch + b"Z")
    add("cp-%04X-mixa" % cp, b"a" + ch + b"z")
    add("cp-%04X-ace" % cp, b"xn--" + ch)
    add("cp-%04X-ACE" % cp, b"XN--" + ch)
    add("cp-%04X-rep" % cp, ch * 5)
    add("cp-%04X-repdot" % cp, (ch + b".") * 4)
    # each individual byte of the encoding, isolated and letter-wrapped
    for i in range(len(ch)):
        add("cp-%04X-b%d" % (cp, i), bytes([ch[i]]))
        add("cp-%04X-b%d-wrapA" % (cp, i), b"A" + bytes([ch[i]]) + b"A")
    # truncated encodings (invalid UTF-8) with letters glued on
    for k in range(1, len(ch)):
        add("cp-%04X-trunc%d" % (cp, k), ch[:k])
        add("cp-%04X-trunc%d-A" % (cp, k), ch[:k] + b"A")
        add("cp-%04X-trunc%d-a" % (cp, k), b"a" + ch[:k] + b"Z")
        add("cp-%04X-tail%d" % (cp, k), ch[k:])
        add("cp-%04X-tail%d-A" % (cp, k), b"A" + ch[k:] + b"B")

# --- 5. Latin-1 / CP1252 single high bytes (uppercase in those charsets) --
for b in range(0xC0, 0x100):
    bb = bytes([b])
    add("latin1-%02x" % b, bb)
    add("latin1-%02x-dom" % b, bb + b".COM")
    add("latin1-%02x-word" % b, b"STRA" + bb + b"E.DE")
# CP1252 upper/lower pairs in the 0x80-0x9f band
for b in range(0x80, 0xA0):
    bb = bytes([b])
    add("cp1252-%02x" % b, bb)
    add("cp1252-%02x-mix" % b, b"Ab" + bb + b"Cd")

# --- 6. full-width alphabet sweeps --------------------------------------
fw_upper = "".join(chr(0xFF21 + i) for i in range(26))
fw_lower = "".join(chr(0xFF41 + i) for i in range(26))
add("fw-upper", fw_upper.encode("utf-8"))
add("fw-lower", fw_lower.encode("utf-8"))
add("fw-mixed", "".join(fw_upper[i] if i % 2 else fw_lower[i]
                        for i in range(26)).encode("utf-8"))
add("fw-upper-dom", fw_upper.encode("utf-8") + b".COM")
add("fw-plus-ascii", fw_upper.encode("utf-8") + b"ABCdef")
add("ascii-plus-fw", b"ABCdef" + fw_lower.encode("utf-8"))
for i in range(26):
    add("fw-single-%d" % i, chr(0xFF21 + i).encode("utf-8"))
    add("fw-single-lo-%d" % i, chr(0xFF41 + i).encode("utf-8"))
    add("fw-single-mix-%d" % i,
        b"X" + chr(0xFF21 + i).encode("utf-8") + b"y")

# --- 7. length boundaries built from case-varying material --------------
for n in (0, 1, 62, 63, 64, 65, 126, 127, 254, 255, 256, 257, 300):
    if n:
        add("len-upper-%d" % n, b"A" * n)
        add("len-lower-%d" % n, b"a" * n)
        add("len-alt-%d" % n, (b"Aa" * ((n + 1) // 2))[:n])
        add("len-high-%d" % n, bytes([0xC3, 0x84] * ((n + 1) // 2))[:n])
        add("len-mix-%d" % n, (b"A\xc3\x84" * ((n + 2) // 3))[:n])
        add("len-fw-%d" % n, (u(0xFF21) * ((n + 2) // 3))[:n])
        add("len-dots-%d" % n, (b"A." * ((n + 1) // 2))[:n])
add("len-empty", b"")

# --- 8. xn-- prefix case permutations ----------------------------------
import itertools
for combo in itertools.product("xX", "nN", "-", "-"):
    p = "".join(combo).encode()
    add("ace-perm-%s" % p.decode(), p)
    add("ace-perm-%s-body" % p.decode(), p + b"Fiq228C")
    add("ace-perm-%s-hi" % p.decode(), p + u(0x00C4) + b".DE")
    add("ace-perm-%s-dbl" % p.decode(), p + p + b"A")
add("ace-short-x", b"x")
add("ace-short-xn", b"xn")
add("ace-short-xn-", b"xn-")
add("ace-only", b"xn--")
add("ace-only-upper", b"XN--")

# --- 9. embedded newlines / quotes / spaces with case ------------------
WEIRD = [b"\n", b"\r", b"\r\n", b"\t", b" ", b'"', b"'", b"\\", b"\x1b",
         b"\x7f", b"\x01", b"\v", b"\f"]
for w in WEIRD:
    add("weird-%s" % w.hex(), w)
    add("weird-%s-up" % w.hex(), b"ABC" + w + b"DEF")
    add("weird-%s-lo" % w.hex(), b"abc" + w + b"def")
    add("weird-%s-hi" % w.hex(), u(0x00C4) + w + u(0x0130))
    add("weird-%s-dom" % w.hex(), b"EX" + w + b"AMPLE.COM")

# --- 10. deterministic pseudo-random mixes -----------------------------
import random
rng = random.Random(0xC45E)
ALPHABET = (
    [bytes([c]) for c in b"AZaz09.-_"] +
    [bytes([c]) for c in (0x80, 0xBF, 0xC0, 0xC3, 0xDF, 0xE0, 0xEF, 0xF0, 0xFF)] +
    [u(cp) for cp in (0x00C4, 0x00DF, 0x0130, 0x0131, 0x01C4, 0x03A3,
                      0x03C2, 0xFF21, 0xFF41, 0x212A, 0x1E9E, 0x10400)] +
    [b"xn--", b"XN--", b"Xn--"]
)
for i in range(700):
    n = rng.randint(1, 22)
    arg = b"".join(rng.choice(ALPHABET) for _ in range(n))
    add("rand-%d" % i, arg)

# --- 11. a handful of multi-arg cases (driver loops over all argv) ------
add("multi-1", b"ABC", b"\xc3\x84", b"xn--Q")
add("multi-2", b"", b"A", b"\xff")
add("multi-3", u(0x0130), u(0x0131), b"SS", b"ss", b"\xdf")
add("multi-4", b"\n", b"A\nB", b"XN--\xc3\x9f")
add("multi-noargs")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- runner

def run(binary, args):
    p = subprocess.run([binary] + args, capture_output=True)
    return p.stdout, p.stderr, p.returncode


def main():
    mismatches = []
    for idx, (label, args) in enumerate(CASES):
        co, ce, cr = run(CPP, args)
        ro, re_, rr = run(RUST, args)
        if co != ro or cr != rr:

            if ce or re_:

    print("TOTAL MISMATCHES: %d" % len(mismatches))
